summary: Nintendo's Excite racing family, from the original side-scrolling motocross game through Vs., Satellaview, Excitebike 64, and Monster Games' Wii-era Excite Truck/Bots/World Rally entries.

entries.title: Excitebike

emulation.emulator: Nintendo 3DS hardware / Citra preservation / NES emulation
emulation.notes: Use owned 3DS copy for 3D Classics; NES emulation or Nintendo Classics is the fallback.

primary.why: The original Excitebike has been re-released many times, but 3D Classics: Excitebike adds stereoscopic 3D, analog support, and expanded custom-track saving while preserving the NES game design. It is the most feature-complete official route for the original.
primary.how_to_play: Play 3D Classics: Excitebike on a Nintendo 3DS/2DS system that already owns it; use Nintendo Switch Online/NES Classic as the simpler fallback.

entries.remaster_caveats: 3D Classics is trapped on the discontinued 3DS eShop ecosystem; new purchases are not available through normal current storefronts.

entries.title: Vs. Excitebike

emulation.emulator: Nintendo Switch / MAME / Famicom Disk System emulator
emulation.notes: Use Switch Arcade Archives for official play; use FDS emulation only for the home variant.

primary.why: Vs. Excitebike is the arcade/Famicom Disk System variant of Excitebike. The Nintendo Switch Arcade Archives release is the current official route for the arcade version, while the Famicom Disk System release remains a historical home variant.
primary.how_to_play: Play Arcade Archives: VS. Excitebike on Nintendo Switch if owned; use Famicom Disk System preservation for that distinct home variant.

secondary.exclusive_content: Japanese home-disk variant of Vs. Excitebike with its own FDS release path.
secondary.what_to_play: Sample the Famicom Disk System version separately if preserving regional variants.
secondary.why: The Switch Arcade Archives release is the clean modern arcade route, but the FDS version is a distinct Japanese home release.

entries.remaster_caveats: Arcade Archives preserves the arcade variant; it does not replace the separate Famicom Disk System home version for regional-variant preservation.

entries.title: BS Excitebike: Bun Bun Mario Battle Stadium

primary.why: BS Excitebike: Bun Bun Mario Battle Stadium is a Satellaview-only Excitebike variant. No modern official port is sourced, so the original Satellaview broadcast/preservation route is the only complete path.
primary.how_to_play: Use preserved Satellaview data in a compatible SNES/Satellaview emulator if available.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official rerelease is sourced; preservation completeness depends on surviving broadcast data.

entries.title: Excitebike 64
entries.definitive_edition: Nintendo Classics release for play; original N64/iQue for branding-complete preservation

emulation.notes: Use Nintendo Classics for official convenience; use original cartridge or N64 emulation for the unaltered branding.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Official Nintendo Classics emulation or N64 emulator upscaling

primary.platform: Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack / Nintendo Classics
primary.why: Excitebike 64 was released for Nintendo 64 and iQue Player, later on Wii U Virtual Console and Nintendo Classics. The Nintendo Classics route is the current official high-accessibility version, though it removes Fox Racing logos, so original N64/iQue hardware remains the branding-complete authenticity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play through Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack/Nintendo Classics; use original N64 or emulator if preserving the original licensed branding matters.

entries.remaster_caveats: Modern Nintendo Classics version removes Fox Racing brand logos.

entries.title: Excite Truck

emulation.notes: Original hardware gives native motion controls; Dolphin can raise resolution with proper controller setup.

primary.why: Excite Truck was released for Wii only and is the third main Excite game, moving the series from motorbikes to off-road trucks. Wii is the only sourced platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original Wii/Wii U hardware or Dolphin with motion-control mapping and internal resolution scaling.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern official rerelease is sourced.

entries.title: Excitebots: Trick Racing

emulation.notes: Original hardware gives native motion controls; Dolphin can raise resolution with proper controller setup.

primary.why: Excitebots: Trick Racing was released for Wii in North America and later Japan via Club Nintendo, with no broader PAL/Australian release sourced. The North American Wii retail disc is the easiest complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the North American Wii disc on original Wii/Wii U hardware or Dolphin; use the Japan Club Nintendo release only for regional preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern official rerelease is sourced; PAL/Australian release was not sourced.

entries.title: Excitebike: World Rally

emulation.emulator: Wii hardware / Dolphin with preserved WiiWare title
emulation.notes: Use an owned installed copy or preservation dump; online features may not be available.

primary.why: Excitebike: World Rally was released only as a WiiWare title for Wii and is the final sourced Excite series entry. It modernizes the classic 2D Excitebike design with 3D graphics, online multiplayer, and a track editor.
primary.how_to_play: Use an owned Wii/Wii U installation or preservation setup; the Wii Shop Channel closure means new purchases are not available.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern official rerelease is sourced; WiiWare availability is limited after Wii Shop Channel closure.
